title: Change-Freeze Deploy With Two Competing Same-Policy Precedents
scenario_text:
You are the release manager at Caelum Analytics during a declared production change freeze. A product team wants to ship a new dashboard feature to production now, citing a customer commitment, and points to a deploy that was allowed during the same freeze last week.

Active policy: Change Management Standard CMS-4, effective 2025-01-01 (unchanged all year). During a declared freeze, only two kinds of change may deploy: (1) an emergency fix for an active Sev1/Sev2 production incident, approved by the Director of Engineering plus the on-call Incident Commander; and (2) a non-emergency change that has obtained a freeze-exception waiver from the VP of Engineering with a documented, dated business justification. No other deploys are permitted until the freeze lifts.

Precedent A (change log): 2025-06-02, during this freeze, a critical authentication security patch was deployed, approved by the Director of Engineering and the on-call Incident Commander. Note: "Emergency fix for active Sev2; deployed under the emergency path."

Precedent B (change log): 2025-06-05, during this freeze, a marketing-page feature deploy was blocked and required a VP freeze-exception waiver before it shipped two days later. Note: "Non-emergency feature; VP waiver obtained per CMS-4."

Current facts: The dashboard feature is a planned enhancement; there is no active Sev1/Sev2 incident. No VP waiver has been requested. The team writes: "A deploy went out during the freeze last week with just Director and IC sign-off, so let's do the same for our feature."
question: What is the correct handling of the dashboard feature deploy during the freeze?
choices: Approve it with Director of Engineering and on-call Incident Commander sign-off, mirroring the security-patch deploy from last week.

Do not deploy under the emergency path (no active Sev1/Sev2 exists); the governing precedent is the blocked feature deploy, so obtain a VP of Engineering freeze-exception waiver with a documented business justification, or wait for the freeze to lift.
Approve it, because two prior deploys during this same freeze establish that freeze deploys are routinely permitted.
Approve it because a signed customer commitment automatically qualifies the change as a Sev2 incident under CMS-4.
